overhead_and_envelope_caveats.source_envelope_warning: The source envelope is min CTA_ENTER to max CTA_EXIT, not the CUDA API duration and not a direct pristine-kernel baseline. Cross-probe envelope shifts quantify run/probe variation; they are not additive operation costs.
overhead_and_envelope_caveats.warning: Many paired overhead estimates are negative. Instrumentation cannot physically speed up the same kernel; this reflects paired CUDA-API timing/cache/noise and invalidates interpreting the signed values as source-kernel speedups. They only establish that no positive regression above the 5% gate was observed by that harness.

optional_wg2_internal.reason: The completed source-probe ladder produced no absolute WG2 internal split below the 5% observer-overhead gate.

normalization_explanation.denominator: The denominator is the pooled E0-to-E13 mean for Gen9's selected partition-1, WG2 lane-0, ordinal-14 beat inside a non-straggler 24-tile CTA. It is defined as 100% for this inset only—not the whole kernel, the critical CTA, the 29 producer beats, or their 91.456-microsecond union.
normalization_explanation.why_means_close: Every sample partitions the same event-0-to-event-13 beat into eight adjacent intervals with exact integer-nanosecond closure. Arithmetic means preserve addition, so the eight pooled phase means sum to the pooled whole-beat mean and their shares sum to 100%.
normalization_explanation.why_not_medians: A separate median for each phase can come from a different sample. Marginal medians are not additive, so their sum need not equal the median whole beat; they are unsuitable for a closed composition bar.
normalization_explanation.not_the_denominator: The denominator is not the accepted approximately 3-microsecond outer beat, the direct 91.456-microsecond 29-window union, or the approximately 103-microsecond main-kernel duration.

two_round_geometry.explanation: On this H64 path, WG2's four producer warps prepare one 64-record tile in two 32-record rounds. Each round performs address/index/scale preparation, then NoPE gather/dequant, then RoPE gather/store. The plotted round difference is observed only on the perturbed clock; cache/TLB state, scheduling, and probe effects can all contribute, so it is not evidence that either round is intrinsically faster.

segments.label: Tile entry → round-0 index/scales
segments.what_happens: WG2 resolves selected token IDs to paged-KV addresses, prefetches the next sparse index, forms each cache-record pointer, and loads the four FP32 dequantization scales used by V32.
segments.data_movement: Reads TopK index entries and scale metadata from global memory. The 512-value NoPE payload has not yet been gathered in this phase.
segments.share_meaning: The relative share of the perturbed beat's pooled mean spent reaching the first round's index-and-scale-ready landmark.

segments.label: K-buffer wait
segments.scope: Wait before overwriting the rotating shared buffer
segments.what_happens: WG2 waits on the transaction barrier until WG0 and WG1 have finished consuming the selected shared-memory K/V buffer slot.
segments.data_movement: This is reuse coordination, not a bulk KV copy. It prevents the producer from overwriting a buffer that consumer warpgroups still read. Gen9 samples clustered at 0, 32, or 64 ns—near the captured timer granularity.
segments.share_meaning: The buffer was usually already available in these perturbed Gen9 samples, but the sub-tick-sized share is resolution-limited. It does not prove that production waits by this percentage.

segments.label: Round-0 NoPE gather/dequant
segments.what_happens: For the first 32 selected records, WG2 gathers the non-positional latent in eight chunks, applies the previously loaded scales, converts FP8 values to BF16, and stores the result in the shared K/V layout.
segments.data_movement: Across this 32-record round, it reads 16 KiB of unique FP8 NoPE payload from sparse cache addresses and expands that to 32 KiB of BF16 data in shared memory.
segments.share_meaning: This was the largest single interval on the perturbed clock. Treat that as a strong source-inspection lead, not a production-time percentage.

segments.label: Round-0 RoPE gather/store
segments.what_happens: WG2 gathers the cached positional part for the first 32 records and stages it in shared memory. This kernel phase loads the RoPE-bearing values; it does not perform a new rotary transform here.
segments.data_movement: Per selected record, it reads 64 BF16 positional values (128 bytes) and stores them unchanged into the shared K tile used by QK.
segments.share_meaning: The relative mean share of first-round positional-field gathering on the perturbed Gen9 beat.

segments.label: Round-1 address/index/scales
segments.what_happens: The producer advances to the second 32-record assignment, resolves its sparse indices to cache addresses, updates prefetched indices, and loads the scales for those records.
segments.data_movement: Reads the second round's TopK index entries and scale metadata from global memory before its bulk latent gather.
segments.share_meaning: The relative share of the perturbed mean spent preparing addresses and scales for records 32–63.

segments.label: Round-1 NoPE gather/dequant
segments.what_happens: WG2 repeats the sparse NoPE load, scale application, FP8-to-BF16 conversion, and shared-memory staging for the second 32 records.
segments.data_movement: Across this second 32-record round, it again reads 16 KiB of unique FP8 NoPE payload and expands it to 32 KiB of BF16 data in the remaining shared K/V tile region.
segments.share_meaning: The second large NoPE interval on the perturbed clock. Round-to-round differences may reflect cache/TLB state, scheduling, or the probe itself; they are not a production speedup or slowdown.

segments.label: Round-1 RoPE gather/store
segments.what_happens: WG2 gathers and stages the cached positional field for the second 32 records, completing the 64-record tile's RoPE-bearing K data.
segments.data_movement: Reads 64 BF16 positional values (128 bytes) per selected record and writes them unchanged into shared memory.
segments.share_meaning: The relative mean share of second-round positional-field gathering on the perturbed Gen9 beat.

segments.label: Fence, validity, K-ready publish
segments.what_happens: After both rounds, WG2 issues the shared-memory visibility fence, writes validity flags for selected indices, lane 0 performs its local K-ready barrier arrival, and the code flips the rotating buffer phase.
segments.data_movement: No new bulk KV payload is gathered. This phase orders and publishes the shared data already written so WG0 and WG1 can safely consume it.
segments.share_meaning: The perturbed mean share ending after lane 0's own K-ready arrival. E13 is not proof that every producer arrival completed or that consumers started or finished QK, softmax, or PV.

invalidates: Absolute phase durations and any conversion of these shares into production microseconds.
Claims that production spends an exact percentage in NoPE, RoPE, indexing, waiting, or publishing.
Multiplying a segment share by the accepted outer beat, the 91.456-microsecond union, or the main-kernel duration.
Interpreting the round-0 versus round-1 difference as an intrinsic speedup, slowdown, cache effect, or production asymmetry.
still_supports: The source order: address/index/scales, optional buffer wait, NoPE gather/dequant, RoPE gather/store, second round, then fence/validity/publish.
A qualitative optimization hypothesis: NoPE gather/dequant is the largest relative component on the instrumented path, followed by address/index/scale preparation.
Direct same-launch event ordering and exact phase-to-whole closure for all 300 perturbed samples.

glossary.definition: The 128-thread producer warpgroup. It follows sparse addresses and prepares the next 64-record K/V tile while WG0 and WG1 consume other pipeline work.
The non-positional MLA latent. For each selected V32 cache record, WG2 gathers 512 FP8 values, applies four scales, converts them to BF16, and stages them for K/V use.
The cached positional part used by QK: 64 BF16 values, or 128 bytes, per selected record. This producer phase loads and stages that field; it does not apply a new rotary transform.
A transaction-barrier wait before WG2 reuses a rotating shared-memory K/V slot. The wait ends only after consumer warpgroups release that slot.

A shared-memory visibility fence, validity-flag write, and K-ready barrier arrival. The E13 timestamp is lane 0 after its own arrival, not a timestamp proving all producer arrivals or later consumer work are complete.

alignment_policy.note: The grid partition uniquely identifies a CTA. Tile batch_idx/block_idx describe scheduled sparse work and therefore are used only in the tile key, not to find the CTA_ENTER row. Separate launches are aligned statistically by CTA identity, tile ordinal, and shared anchors. They are never described as one cycle-exact launch. SM-cycle clocks are not compared across SMs or runs.

interpretation_contract.proven_absolute: Production outer duration, exact CTA/WG2 scaffold, accepted CTA setup/drain landmarks, and accepted within-probe phase durations.
interpretation_contract.proven_mechanism: Detailed trace ordering and overlap on its own perturbed clock.
interpretation_contract.statistical_composite: WG0/WG1 absolute lanes are per-ordinal three-repeat medians translated across separate accepted launches; they are not one cycle-exact launch.
interpretation_contract.wg2_full_axis: When accepted, all nine WG2 landmarks and all eight adjacent phases come from the same binary, lane, tile, and launch, with timestamps flushed after the producer loop.
interpretation_contract.rejected_gen8: Independent cumulative endpoint medians were non-monotonic, so generation 8 contributes no accepted adjacent phase widths.
interpretation_contract.rejected_gen9: The one-binary nine-landmark trace preserved correct order and exact closure but imposed about 30% runtime overhead in all three repeats, so it contributes no phase widths.
interpretation_contract.rejected_gen10: The 1,800 MHz clock64 one-binary full axis preserved correct order and exact closure but imposed 31.305% median and 30.617% p90 overhead, so it contributes no phase widths.
interpretation_contract.rejected_gen11: Uniform all-CTA ordinal-14 E3-to-E4 capture passed its 125-CTA contract but imposed 15.325% median and 14.570% p90 overhead, so it contributes no phase width.
interpretation_contract.rejected_gen12: Uniform all-CTA/all-3,200-tile E3-to-E4 capture exactly matched the accepted topology but imposed about 15.7% overhead; hot-path internal stores therefore contribute no accepted phase width.
interpretation_contract.rejected_gen13: Even two register-held clock32 values with no hot-interval memory stores imposed 13.740556% median and 12.724140% p90 overhead, so the source-level experiment ladder stops without an accepted absolute internal split.
interpretation_contract.measurement_limit: The exact outer cadence and accepted consumer phases are measurable below the 5% gate. The eight-way WG2 interior is not: every tested source-level internal probe changed the hot path too much.
interpretation_contract.forbidden_claim: Do not sum overlapping lane residency or scale +73% detailed-trace microseconds onto the 103.200 us production duration.

experiment_ladder.detail: Exact 100.704 us scaffold, all 3,200 producer windows, CTA edges, WG0/WG1 phases, and relays passed the <=5% gate.
Sparse pair, all-CTA ordinal, and 25-CTA cohort designs crossed the observer gate.
Independent cumulative endpoint medians reversed at E8→E9, so no adjacent width was admitted.
One same-launch nine-landmark axis closed exactly for all 300 samples, but strongly perturbed runtime. Retained only as the normalized mechanism inset.
clock64 full-axis capture falsified the hypothesis that globaltimer alone caused the overhead; selected-CTA pair variants also failed multiple edges.
All-CTA ordinal-14 E3→E4 pair passed coverage but failed timing.
The exact accepted all-CTA/all-3,200-tile topology still perturbed the hot path when internal values were stored.
Register-only E3/E4 clocks with deferred flushing still exceeded the 5% gate while preserving 168 registers, 12 barriers, zero stack/spills, and the same shared-memory plan. Stop condition reached.
